bioprojects.title: Cuora mccordi isolate:ISIS 951048 Genome sequencing and assembly

description.comment: McCord's box turtle is a critically endangered box turtle endemic to central Guangxi province, China. The species was described as recent as 1988 and only known from the pet trade and Chinese food markets. Almost 20 years later specimens were discovered in the wild. This species is being sequenced by John Bermingham in cooperation with the C. mccordi St. Louis Zoo (Missouri) breeding program. Genomic and RNAseq reads are submitted to produce an annotated assembly for the STL breeding program.
description.title: Model organism or animal sample from Cuora mccordi

assembly_info.comments:
The McCord's box turtle DNA was derived from blood of a single male (ISIS no. 951048) at the Saint Louis Zoo, Saint Louis, MO. The turtle has a zoo ID of C. mccordi 4. Sequences were generated on the 10X Genomics Chromium sequencing platform to a
71X coverage based on a genome size of 2.6Gb. The sequences were assembled by the de novo assembly program, Supernova v2.1.1. Of the 2.6 Gb assembled genome (C_mccordi-1.0), the total assembly N50 contig and scaffold lengths are 74.3 kb and 32.6 Mb, respectively. For questions regarding this C_mccordi-1.0 assembly please contact Robert Fulton, McDonnell Genome Institute at Washington University School of Medicine, St. Louis.
Data use: The C_mccordi-1.0 assembly sequence is made freely available to the community by the McDonnell Genome Institute at Washington University School of Medicine, with the following understanding: 1. The data may be freely downloaded, used in analyses, and repackaged in databases. 2. Users are free to use the data in scientific papers analyzing these data if the providers of these data are properly cited. 3. Any redistribution of the data should carry this notice.
